title: Two-stage learned model forecasts hydrogen dispersion from early sensor observations
summary: An MLP ensemble estimated leak rate from early sensor readings, then a sparse Gaussian-process model predicted hydrogen concentration in a confined-channel dataset. The dataset combined 22 physical release tests and 10 CFD cases, representing 26 unique scenarios. Reported leak-rate MAE was 0.052 g/s; the selected dispersion model had concentration-volume-fraction MAE 0.0176 and RMSE 0.0226 on four test experiments. Candidate models were compared on that test set before final selection. This retrospective proof of concept does not establish ship-compartment transfer, operational safety benefit or prospective performance.
ai_technology: MLP ensemble; sparse variational Gaussian process with Beta likelihood
organization: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: Existing channel-release sensor/CFD data were used for scenario-based training and evaluation. Seven MLPs estimated leak rate; the final SVGP model had MAE 0.0176/RMSE 0.0226 in concentration volume-fraction units. Four held-out test experiments also supported uncertainty-coverage analysis, but their performance influenced final model selection.
evidence.unknown: One simplified channel geometry and few scenarios; high-flow cases had larger errors. No deployed ship-compartment or prospective safety benefit was demonstrated. Test-set candidate selection limits the interpretation as an untouched final performance estimate. A later journal DOI has January 2027 issue metadata; its online version date was not established here.
evidence.ai_role: A learned MLP ensemble maps early sensor history to unknown release rate; a learned Gaussian-process regressor uses that estimate, position and time to predict concentration and uncertainty.
